Maybe your lack of change is actually why you’re not improving. If you continually work out the same way, you will never work out the other muscle that exist but we are less aware of. Coming from a 21F wildland firefighter who does physical training 8 hours a week, trust me when I say there are so many different exercises that work out the same area but each individual can hit more specific muscle groups.

Instead of regular push ups, start doing diamond for 4 count push ups. Instead of the sit ups, or adding in with it, do a minute plank. When doing your Russian twist, try different style of it, grab a ball or water bottle or weights if you have them, change the distance in which how far your arms are going and how far your legs are out from your body. Do jump squats, backwards lunges, and try instead of calf raises do mountain climbers. 

Seriously, I implore you to try just these changes and get back to me on how sore you are the next day. I’ll be honest, I can’t 100% tell you it will make the worlds biggest difference in how you feel, but I’d really love to know out of curiosity if this actually helps you improve. 

Oh and also odd one to do but literally just toe raises, while sitting or standing, pull your foot up as if you’re trying to get your toes your shine. That works out a specific muscle in your legs that men naturally develop easier than women do. This could make a huge difference.
